title: Injective representatives of resolution roofs and their canonical transposes
statement:
Let $\mathcal B,\mathcal E$ be abelian categories in the universes of [def-sp-abelian, def-weil-size-convention], with ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and suppose $\mathcal E$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $L:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$ be exact and additive, with a specified additive right adjoint $R$. Use the canonical derived adjunction and canonical shift comparison of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction, lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift]. Fix $X\in\mathcal B$, $N\in\mathcal E$, a cochain complex $P$ vanishing in positive degrees, a quasi-isomorphism $e:P\to LX[0]$, a nonnegative injective resolution $a:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], an integer $q\geq0$, and a cochain map $u:P\to N[q]$.

There exists a cochain map $h:LX[0]\to I[q]$ such that $he$ is chain-homotopic to $a[q]u$ and
$$Q(h)=Q(a[q])Q(u)Q(e)^{-1}.$$
For every such $h$, let $\widetilde h:X[0]\to R(I[q])$ be its termwise adjoint. Under the canonical shift identification, its component in degree zero defines a map $\widetilde h^{\flat}:X[-q]\to R(I^\bullet)$. If $\beta_a:Q R(I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R R(N[0])$ is the canonical injective-resolution identification, then
$$\beta_a Q(\widetilde h^{\flat})=\Phi_q\bigl(Q(u)Q(e)^{-1}\bigr),$$
where $\Phi_q$ is the canonical derived-adjunction bijection followed by the canonical shift identification. This holds for every choice of $a,h$ above, without projectivity of any $P^i$. For internal equivariant modules, exact trivial inflation and invariants as in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module, lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] instantiate $L,R$; in that case the termwise adjoint is the unique factorization of $h$ through the invariant inclusion.

proof.text: Put $J=I[q]$. Its terms are injective, and $J^n=0$ for $n<-q$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] makes $J$ K-injective. Set $f=Q(u)Q(e)^{-1}$ and $v=Q(a[q])f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], localization gives a bijection from homotopy classes of maps $LX[0]\to J$ to derived maps $Q(LX[0])\to QJ$. Choose a representative $h$ of the class corresponding to $v$. Then $Q(he)=vQ(e)=Q(a[q]u)$. Apply the injective part of the same bijection with source $P$ and target $J$: $he$ and $a[q]u$ are homotopic. This proves both the existence and the displayed formula for $Q(h)$. The bijection allows an arbitrary source complex, so no bounded-below or projectivity condition on $P$ has been used.

For any $h$ satisfying the required homotopy, the same localization calculation gives $Qh=Q(a[q])f$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to $X[0]$ and $J$: its transpose is the chain map $\widetilde h=R(h)\eta_{X[0]}$. In degree zero this is $R(h^0)\eta_X:X\to R(I^q)$; all other source components vanish. The chain condition says $(-1)^qR(d_I^q)\widetilde h^0=0$, equivalently $R(d_I^q)\widetilde h^0=0$. Hence the same component defines the chain map $\widetilde h^{\flat}:X[-q]\to R(I)$. Shifting a chain map shifts its components without multiplying them by a sign, so shifting $\widetilde h$ by $[-q]$ and using the termwise shift identification gives precisely $\widetilde h^{\flat}$.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, termwise homotopy adjunction in its proof; component calculation written by Q36.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha_T:Q(RT)\to\mathbf R R(QT)$ for the universal right-derived comparison. The Grothendieck hypothesis supplies K-injective resolutions by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]; [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] makes $\alpha_J$ invertible. Use the unbounded adjunction of [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization], taking the left resolving class to be all complexes: exactness of $L$ makes termwise $L$ invert quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], so $D(L)$ with its invertible comparison $\varphi$ is a universal left derived pair. Denote its unshifted Hom bijection by $\Psi$. Its stated normalization, with $\varphi$ inserted, gives
$$\Psi(Qh)=\alpha_JQ(\widetilde h).$$
This adjunction is the canonical one of the statement, because the normalization determines it. For a complex $M$ of $\mathcal B$ and a K-injective $J'$, every derived map $Q(LM)\to QJ'$ is $Q$ of a chain map by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $\varphi$ is invertible, and every object of $D(\mathcal E)$ is isomorphic to such a $QJ'$ by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]; naturality in the second variable then fixes $\Psi$ on all pairs. Applied to the identity chain map of $LM$, the normalization is the canonical unit formula $\mathbf RR(\varphi_M)\eta^D_{QM}=\alpha_{LM}Q(\eta_M)$, and an adjunction between given functors is determined by its unit, so no adjunction transported by an automorphism satisfies it.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors, with Tag 0FND, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, ordinary-transpose normalization; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined.

proof.text:
Naturality of the adjunction bijection in its target and $Qh=Q(a[q])f$ now give
$$\mathbf R R(Q(a[q]))\Psi(f)=\Psi(Qh)=\alpha_JQ(\widetilde h).$$
Invert $\mathbf R R(Q(a[q]))$ and put
$$\beta_{a[q]}=\mathbf R R(Q(a[q]))^{-1}\alpha_J.$$
Consequently $\Psi(f)=\beta_{a[q]}Q(\widetilde h)$. This is the canonical injective-resolution identification: it maps the specified augmentation by the derived functor and then inverts it, using the derived comparison on the injective target. This formula follows directly from the unit normalization of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], so there is no choice of a comparison on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0FND, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, functoriality in the target; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined, normalized resolution comparison.

proof.text:
Apply the canonical shift compatibility of [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift]. It identifies $\Psi(f):QX[0]\to\mathbf R R(Q(N[q]))$ with the map $\Phi_q(f):Q(X[-q])\to\mathbf R R(QN[0])$ in the statement. Under the same compatibility $\beta_{a[q]}$ is the $[q]$-shift of $\beta_a=\mathbf R R(Qa)^{-1}\alpha_I$: these comparisons use the shifted augmentation $a[q]$ and the fixed K-injective shift, which the cited statement explicitly retains. Concretely, $I$ and $I[q]$ are K-injective (step 1), so on $QI$ the fixed K-injective shift isomorphism of $\mathbf RR$ is the one under which $\alpha_{I[q]}$ corresponds to $\alpha_I[q]$ through the termwise equality $R(I[q])=R(I)[q]$; the shift isomorphisms of $\mathbf RR$ and $Q$ are natural, so $\mathbf RR(Q(a[q]))$ corresponds to $\mathbf RR(Qa)[q]$. Thus shifting the equality in step 4 by $[-q]$, and using the component identification of step 2, gives
$$\Phi_q(f)=\beta_aQ(\widetilde h^{\flat}).$$
Every comparison used here is the fixed canonical one; the degree-$q$ component is $R(h^0)\eta_X$, with no additional scalar or shift sign.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact, and Tag 0DVC, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors; canonical K-injective shift compatibility supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] states that the internal action categories are Grothendieck abelian and that exact trivial-action inflation is left adjoint to invariants, with transpose given by the invariant inclusion. It therefore supplies exactly the hypotheses on $L,R$ used above. Since the source of $h$ has trivial action, its equivariance means that $h$ factors through the invariant subobject of $I[q]$; the adjunction identifies this factorization with $\widetilde h$. Uniqueness follows because the invariant inclusion is a monomorphism. The proof used only the prescribed properties of $a$ and $h$, so it applies to every such choice, including $q=0$.
